This is a safe plan that fits the physio's limits. It has exactly three walk-run days (Mon/Wed/Sat), each with a day off running in between, so the shin gets recovery. Each session is short: 16 min, with 5 rounds of 2 min easy running and 1 min walking, about 10 min of running in total. The heart-rate cap of 135 keeps it easy. The two other days are the physio's calf and hip routine, which is sensible. Next to a 5.1 km week this is a modest step, so the returning runner isn't rushed and the volume doesn't jump. The opening reassures Ines about her nerves by pointing to real signs that the restart went well, which fits her "nervous but happy" note.

Why it isn't a 5: none of the lines I can see repeats the physio's rule to stop if the shin aches. For a runner coming back from a stress reaction, that rule belongs in the plan in plain words. The draft also cites 0/10 pain and heart rates of 121–123 bpm against a 178 ceiling, none of which are on the card. They are probably from her logged data, but I couldn't check them. Finally, it gives no sense of how this week moves her toward 30 minutes of continuous running by mid-October.
